title: A Security Games Inspired Approach for Distributed Control of Pandemic Spread
short_title: Security Games Inspired Distributed Control of Pandemic Spread
abstract: Pandemics are a source of extensive mortality, economic impairment, and dramatic social fluctuation. Once a pandemic occurs, policymakers are faced with the highly challenging task of controlling it over time and space. In this article, a novel pandemic intervention policy that relies on the strategic deployment of inspection units (IUs) is proposed. These IUs are allocated in the environment, represented as a graph, and sample individuals who pass through the same node. If a sampled individual is identified as infected, she is extracted from the environment until she recovers (or dies). A realistic simulation‐based evaluation of the Influenza A pathogen using both synthetic and real‐world data is provided. The results demonstrate potential significant benefits of the proposed PIP in mitigating a pandemic spread which can complement other standard policies such as social distancing and mask-wearing.
summary: Once a pandemic starts, policymakers must control it over time and space. Taking inspiration from security games, we propose an intervention policy that strategically places inspection units on a graph representing the environment; the units sample people passing through, and those found infected are removed until they recover or die. Realistic simulations of Influenza A with synthetic and real-world data show potential significant benefits for mitigating spread, complementing measures such as social distancing and mask-wearing.
key_findings: We propose a pandemic intervention policy based on strategically deploying inspection units that sample individuals passing through nodes of a graph.
Sampled individuals identified as infected are extracted from the environment until they recover or die.
Simulations of Influenza A using synthetic and real-world data show potential significant benefits in mitigating pandemic spread.
The policy can complement standard policies such as social distancing and mask-wearing.
